selected.description: When a user mentions doing an activity with their pet (e.g., walking, hiking), during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement where the speaker describes performing an activity with their pet as a candidate memory, even if it appears in casual sign-off or small talk.
Record the activity and the pet name as the object (e.g., 'walks with Buddy', 'hikes with Toby'), with the speaker as the subject.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp; if the activity is described as a general habit, capture it as a state; if it is a one-off event, capture it as an event.
Stop after capturing the stated activity; do not infer additional pet facts or unrelated activities unless explicitly mentioned.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Relational Framing
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how they view a person, pet, or group (e.g., 'pets are family', 'feel like family'), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly declares how they view someone or something (e.g., 'pets are family', 'my little family', 'feel like family', 'as a friend'), create a separate profile or relationship memory capturing that view, even if the message also contains event details like photos or activities.
Use memory kind 'relationship' when the statement defines a connection between the speaker and the subject; otherwise use 'state' or 'preference' for attitudes and values.
Apply to both first mentions and repeated mentions across sessions; record the view as a durable memory rather than folding it into an event memory.
Only extract when the framing is explicit or strongly implied; do not infer relationships from generic pleasantries, compliments, or small talk.
Stop after capturing the explicit view in one memory per stated relationship; do not add redundant memories for every photo or activity that merely implies the same view.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Specific Plan Details in Event Memory Extraction
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting an event or plan memory and messages state what participants will try, do, or consume, include those concrete details in the memory content.
content: During extraction of event/plan memories, if messages explicitly state what participants will try, do, or consume (e.g., a specific dish, drink, or activity), preserve those concrete items in the memory content instead of replacing them with a generic label like 'date' or 'meet up'.
When the same plan is mentioned across multiple messages, merge the explicitly stated specifics into one memory record, but do not add details that were not said.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.
